correctness.rationale: The minimum geodesic gap equals the minimum nonzero affine Voronoi power margin. Six signed vectors suffice for every nonnegative threshold on the shear family because six adjacent unimodular cones have pairwise nonnegative generator inner products, implying every other margin constraint. The area-preserving coordinate image is exactly a rectangle minus two right triangles. The all-lattice strip derivative and conditional mark law follow from facet-normal coordinates and O(epsilon squared) vertex neighborhoods. Cauchy identity plus the six-side polygonal isoperimetric inequality gives the exact nonnegative defect and unique triangular equality. The packaged exact-rational checker passed 108 independently clipped finite-vector comparisons; finite checking is corroborative, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The observable measures how close a random displacement is to having two minimizing geodesics, a natural ambiguity statistic in cut-locus geometry and nearest-lattice-point quantization. An entire shear-moduli CDF exhibits a sharp six-to-four-facet transition and a non-differentiable square limit; the arbitrary-lattice coefficient has an exact isoperimetric defect and a uniquely optimal equilateral torus. Conditional facet marks identify where near ties occur. These structural and inverse-shape distinctions go beyond a routine scalar probability exercise.
